external_threshold.source: Seattle SDCI task threshold fixed a priori: EstProjectCost at least 50000 nominal USD and a 48 calendar-month completion horizon from IssuedDate.

measurements.frame: Applicant-declared fair-market construction cost in nominal USD; population floor and feature.
Binary forward outcome from CompletedDate relative to IssuedDate plus 48 calendar months.

task.question: Will a newly issued Seattle building permit for a substantive construction project reach final inspection sign-off within four years of issuance?
task.population: Every row in the live Socrata snapshot with PermitTypeMapped equal to Building, IssuedDate in the half-open window 2016-01-01 through 2022-10-01, and EstProjectCost at least 50000 nominal USD. Rows with impossible chronology (CompletedDate before IssuedDate, or IssuedDate before AppliedDate when both are present) are excluded as a source data-quality rule per the construction recipe. The unit is the permit as issued; no site-level or contractor-level aggregates are used. The population is fixed by permit type, issuance date and declared cost, not by the label value.
task.prediction_time: The permit IssuedDate, when the permit is issued. Only fields written at submittal, during plan review, or at issuance are used; CompletedDate, StatusCurrent, ExpiresDate and post-issuance revisions are excluded from features. The label is observed retrospectively after the 48-month window.
task.usefulness: The label is a four-year forward final-inspection sign-off that does not exist at issuance. Completion is the majority class (about 76-84 percent depending on cohort; non-completion about 16-24 percent), so the task is to separate the substantial stalling minority from projects that close out. It speaks to construction-pipeline attrition and permit-expiry workload. Because rows are single permits and no prior-permit history is used, the task is retrospective and row-local.
task.simple_references: Majority-class control predicting completed for every row is 76-84 percent accurate depending on cohort. Calendar control uses issuance month only. Identity and structure control uses permit class, permit type and ZIP only. Persistence does not apply: each row is a single issuance event with no prior state inside the row, and prior-permit history is deliberately excluded; the nearest analogue is the class-group base rate already covered by the identity control.

prediction_instant.citation: Permit IssuedDate is the event time; the Socrata resource is a daily-refreshed current snapshot with no reporting-period publication schedule.

row_selection.rule: Select Building permits with IssuedDate in [2016-01-01, 2022-10-01) and EstProjectCost at least 50000 nominal USD; exclude rows with impossible chronology (CompletedDate before IssuedDate, or IssuedDate before AppliedDate when both dates are present). This is an event-time eligibility rule with a disclosed data-quality exclusion, not a historical forecasting claim.

cross_row_audit.auxiliary_files_review: Only public/train.csv, public/eval.csv and private/holdout.csv are written; no fixture labels, answer scaffolds or auxiliary evaluation files.
cross_row_audit.rationale: All features are row-local. No cross-row contractor history, prior-permit outcomes or site aggregates are used. Sibling permits may share ParentPermitNum or RelatedMUP, so rows are not strictly independent, but those flags are row-local.

limitations: The outcome is an administrative final-inspection completion record, not occupancy or certificate of occupancy. A physically finished project whose final inspection was never logged counts as non-completion.

A null CompletedDate is documented as generally still under inspection; the frozen task maps null to y=0. This is an evidenced field interpretation, not an assumption that an unknown outcome is negative after the 48-month window.
The Socrata resource is a live daily-refreshed current snapshot with no immutable archive. Exact population counts are tied to the 2026-11-14 publisher evidence and may fail on a later refresh.
There is no full-row historical availability ledger. Feature availability at issuance is assumed from field semantics and current-snapshot presence, not proven.
Plan-review and housing-unit fields have substantial missingness. Missing numeric and token values are left blank, not filled with zero.
EstProjectCost is mutable and is used both for population eligibility and as a feature, so a few projects may enter the cohort retrospectively after an upward revision.
Rows may be correlated across sibling permits through ParentPermitNum or RelatedMUP; no site-level independence is claimed.
The 2021-2022 holdout sits in a different construction-cost and post-pandemic regime than the training years. This is part of the task, not an artefact to remove.
ExpiresDate is mechanically IssuedDate plus about 18 months and is not used as a feature.
Same-day CompletedDate values occur; they are kept because the field rule is unambiguous, but they depress the informativeness of the positive class.

selection.evidence: PermitTypeMapped, IssuedDate and EstProjectCost are fixed before or at issuance. Rows with impossible chronology are removed as a source data-quality rule; no row is selected because its label is positive or negative.
selection.rule: Building permits with IssuedDate in [2016-01-01, 2022-10-01) and EstProjectCost at least 50000 nominal USD; exclude CompletedDate before IssuedDate or IssuedDate before AppliedDate when both dates are present.

vintage.evidence: Live Socrata endpoint; publisher metadata states the snapshot was last updated 2026-11-14 and there is no immutable archive.

construction_notes: The download uses the actual Socrata CSV resource with an explicit column list and a date/cost filter. Permit type is deliberately not filtered in the download so non-Building codes in the date/cost slice are counted and then excluded by the frozen population. The population and label are fixed: Building permits issued in [2016-01-01, 2022-10-01), EstProjectCost at least 50000 nominal USD, y=1 only when CompletedDate is non-null and no later than IssuedDate plus 48 calendar months; null CompletedDate maps to y=0 per the portal documentation that it generally means still under inspection. Impossible chronology rows are dropped per the source construction recipe and their count is returned in a check. Features are row-local; the top-20 ZIP mapping is fitted on training rows only, issue month is encoded as sine and cosine, and missing values remain blank rather than zero. No label-derived rates, prior-permit outcomes, holdout-based feature choices or post-outcome fields are shipped. Checks cover exact publisher population counts, two concrete sample permits, cost-floor and 48-month unit checks, unique permit IDs, binary labels, output headers, split-window integrity and training feature coverage. Missing semantic evidence: there is no full historical availability ledger, only a current snapshot; plan-review fields are frequently missing; exact population checks are tied to the 2026-11-14 publisher evidence and may fail on later source drift. No persistence score column exists because each row is a single issuance event with no prior state inside the row, so references is null with identity columns permitclass, permitclassmapped, permittypedesc and originalzip. Quality descriptions correct the source narrative: completion is the majority class at roughly 76-84 percent and non-completion is the 16-24 percent minority, while the target positive label remains completion within 48 months.
